subject: sst
prompt_en: How many languages are listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution?
prompt_hi: Constitution ki Eighth Schedule mein kitni bhashayein listed hain?

subject: sst
prompt_en: Explain to a visitor from abroad what 'many in the one' means in India, with two examples.
prompt_hi: Videsh se aaye mehmaan ko samjhao ki Bharat mein 'ek mein anek' ka kya matlab hai, do examples ke saath.
answer: India has many languages, foods, dresses and festivals, but shared threads join them — e.g. one harvest celebrated as Pongal, Bihu and Lohri, or the Ramayana retold in many languages; diversity is kept and respected, not erased.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name three ways family members support one another.
prompt_hi: Parivaar ke log ek-doosre ki madad kin 3 tareekon se karte hain?
answer: Any three: caring for children and elders, sharing housework, earning and sharing money, teaching skills and values, comforting in hard times, celebrating together.

subject: sst
prompt_en: List all the work done in your home in one day. Who does each task? Suggest one change that would make it fairer.
prompt_hi: Ek din mein ghar mein hone wala saara kaam list karo. Kaun kya karta hai? Ise zyada fair banane ke liye ek badlaav batao.
answer: Any honest list with one reasonable fair-sharing change (e.g., children fold clothes or fill water bottles; tasks rotated so no one person does everything).

subject: sst
prompt_en: A boy says: 'Cooking and cleaning are not my job — only Mummy's.' What is wrong with this thinking?
prompt_hi: Ek ladka kehta hai: 'Khana banana aur safai mera kaam nahi — sirf Mummy ka hai.' Is soch mein kya galat hai?
answer: Home work is for the whole family to share according to age and ability; everyone eats and uses the home, so everyone can help.

subject: sst
prompt_en: In a gurdwara langar, anyone can sit and eat for free, and volunteers cook and serve. How does this show a community supporting people?
prompt_hi: Gurdwara ke langar mein koi bhi baith kar muft khana kha sakta hai, aur sevadaar khana banate-parosate hain. Yeh samudaay ki madad kaise dikhata hai?
answer: People share work voluntarily to feed everyone equally, whoever they are — caring for others beyond one's own family.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: a flood hits a village. What would happen if every family only looked after itself, compared with neighbours helping each other?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek gaon mein baadh aa jaati hai. Agar har parivaar sirf apna dhyaan rakhe, aur agar padosi ek-doosre ki madad karein — dono mein kya hoga?
answer: Alone, weaker families (elders, sick, poor) would suffer more and recovery would be slow; together, people share food, shelter and work, rescue each other and recover faster.

subject: sst
prompt_en: What does 'vasudhaiva kutumbakam' mean, and why is it an important idea today?
prompt_hi: 'Vasudhaiva kutumbakam' ka kya matlab hai, aur aaj yeh vichaar kyon zaroori hai?
answer: It means 'the world is one family'; today countries and people depend on each other (for food, climate, health, trade), so caring for all people like family helps everyone.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare how a family and a community help people. Give one thing only a family usually does and one thing a community does better.
prompt_hi: Parivaar aur samudaay logon ki madad kaise karte hain, compare karo. Ek kaam jo aam taur pe sirf parivaar karta hai aur ek jo samudaay behtar karta hai.
answer: Family: daily personal care, raising children, emotional closeness at home. Community: big shared tasks like cleaning a pond, organising festivals, community kitchens, help in disasters.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name two age-appropriate tasks a Class 6 student can do to share home responsibilities.
prompt_hi: Class 6 ka student ghar ki zimmedariyan baantne ke liye kaun se do kaam kar sakta hai?
answer: Any two suitable tasks: making the bed, folding clothes, laying the table, watering plants, sorting waste, helping younger siblings with homework, filling water bottles.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Draw (or describe) circles of care: you in the middle, then family, then neighbours, then town, then the world. Write one way of helping in each circle.
prompt_hi: Dekhbhaal ke circles banao (ya batao): beech mein tum, phir parivaar, padosi, sheher aur duniya. Har circle mein madad ka ek tareeka likho.
answer: Any sensible example per ring, e.g., family: help with chores; neighbours: share food at festivals; town: join a cleanliness drive; world: save water and electricity for the planet.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name two things that families pass on from one generation to the next.
prompt_hi: Do cheezein batao jo parivaar ek peedhi se doosri peedhi tak pahunchate hain.
answer: Any two: values, stories, language, skills (cooking, farming, crafts), traditions and festivals, recipes.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Explain to a younger child how families and communities help people, and why sharing work fairly matters.
prompt_hi: Chhote bachche ko samjhao ki parivaar aur samudaay logon ki madad kaise karte hain, aur kaam ko fair tareeke se baantna kyon zaroori hai.
answer: Families (of many kinds) care for each other, share work and pass on values; communities help through shared work, festivals, community kitchens and help in hard times; fair sharing by everyone by age and ability is kinder and makes life easier for all; the world can be one family.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name the three organs of government and say in one word what each does.
prompt_hi: Sarkaar ke 3 ang batao aur har ek ka kaam ek shabd mein.
answer: Legislature — makes laws; executive — implements (carries out) laws; judiciary — judges/settles disputes and interprets laws.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why is it a good idea that the people who make laws are different from those who judge disputes?
prompt_hi: Yeh achha vichaar kyon hai ki kaanoon banane wale log aur vivaad ka faisla karne wale log alag hon?
answer: So that no single group has all the power; judges can check whether laws and actions are fair and lawful, protecting people from misuse of power.

subject: sst
prompt_en: In a school, the student council writes the class rules, the monitor makes sure they are followed, and the teacher settles quarrels. Match each to an organ of government.
prompt_hi: School mein student council class ke niyam banati hai, monitor dhyaan rakhta hai ki niyam maane jaayein, aur teacher jhagde suljhaate hain. Har ek ko sarkaar ke ang se milao.
answer: Student council = legislature; monitor = executive; teacher (settling quarrels) = judiciary.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Match each problem to a level of government: (a) the army and defence, (b) a broken village handpump, (c) state police.
prompt_hi: Har samasya ko sarkaar ke star se milao: (a) sena aur raksha, (b) gaon ka toota handpump, (c) rajya police.
answer: (a) Union (national), (b) local (gram panchayat), (c) state.

subject: sst
prompt_en: A student writes: 'In a democracy, people's only job is to vote; after that they have no say.' Correct this.
prompt_hi: Ek student ne likha: 'Democracy mein logon ka ek hi kaam hai vote dena; uske baad unki koi baat nahi.' Ise theek karo.
answer: Citizens take part all the time: attending meetings like gram sabhas, raising complaints, questioning leaders, discussing issues peacefully and holding leaders accountable — voting is only one part.

subject: sst
prompt_en: The Uttaramerur inscriptions in Tamil Nadu, about 1,100 years old, describe something about village life. What do they describe?
prompt_hi: Tamil Nadu ke Uttaramerur shilalekh, lagbhag 1,100 saal puraane, gaon ki zindagi ke baare mein kya batate hain?
answer: Rules for choosing members of village assemblies and committees, including drawing names written on palm leaves from a pot.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: what might happen if the government official who builds a road could also be the only judge of complaints about that road?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar sadak banane wala sarkaari adhikari hi us sadak ki shikayaton ka akela judge bhi ho, to kya ho sakta hai?
answer: Complaints might be ignored or unfairly decided, since the official would be judging their own work — that is why judging is kept separate.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Think of one problem on your street or in your school. Which level of government would handle it, and how could you as a citizen raise it?
prompt_hi: Apni gali ya school ki ek samasya socho. Kaunsa star ki sarkaar ise sambhaalegi, aur tum ek naagrik ki tarah ise kaise uthaa sakte ho?
answer: Any correct match (local for drains, streetlights, garbage; state for state roads, state-run schools) plus a real way to raise it (complaint to panchayat/ward office, helpline or app, letter, speaking at a gram sabha or ward meeting).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Turn this into a flow chart: a new rule about plastic bags is made, shops are checked, and a shopkeeper who disagrees with a fine goes to court.
prompt_hi: Isse flow chart mein badlo: plastic bags ka naya niyam banta hai, dukaanon ki jaanch hoti hai, aur fine se asahmat dukaandaar court jaata hai.
answer: Legislature makes the rule → executive (officials) checks shops and fines → judiciary (court) hears the shopkeeper and decides.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare a democracy with rule by a single king: who makes decisions, and what can ordinary people do in each?
prompt_hi: Democracy aur ek raja ke shasan ko compare karo: faisle kaun leta hai, aur aam log har ek mein kya kar sakte hain?
answer: Democracy: elected representatives decide, people vote, take part, question and can change leaders through elections; single-ruler rule: the king decides, and people usually cannot choose or remove him.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Teach a friend what 'governance' means and how the three organs of government share power.
prompt_hi: Ek dost ko sikhao ki 'governance' ka matlab kya hai aur sarkaar ke 3 ang taakat kaise baant-te hain.
answer: Governance is how a society is run — making rules, carrying them out, providing services and settling disputes; the legislature makes laws, the executive carries them out, the judiciary settles disputes and interprets laws; keeping them separate stops misuse of power; it happens at Union, state and local levels.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Who can be a member of the gram sabha?
prompt_hi: Gram sabha ka sadasya kaun ban sakta hai?
answer: Every adult aged 18 or above whose name is on the voters' list of that panchayat area.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare the gram sabha and the gram panchayat: who is in each, and what does each do?
prompt_hi: Gram sabha aur gram panchayat ko compare karo: har ek mein kaun hai, aur har ek kya karta hai?
answer: Gram sabha: all adult voters of the area; it discusses, approves plans and checks the panchayat's work. Gram panchayat: elected panch members and sarpanch; it carries out the work day to day.

subject: sst
prompt_en: For how many years is a gram panchayat elected, and what is its head called?
prompt_hi: Gram panchayat kitne saal ke liye chuni jaati hai, aur uske mukhiya ko kya kehte hain?
answer: Five years; the head is the sarpanch (also called pradhan or mukhiya).

subject: sst
prompt_en: The village handpump is broken and the school needs a toilet. Where should villagers raise this, and who carries out the work?
prompt_hi: Gaon ka handpump kharab hai aur school ko toilet chahiye. Gaon wale yeh baat kahaan uthayein, aur kaam kaun karega?
answer: Raise it at the gram sabha (or with the gram panchayat); the gram panchayat plans and carries out the work using its funds or government schemes.

subject: sst
prompt_en: A student says: 'The government appoints the sarpanch, and the panchayat secretary is elected by villagers.' Fix the mistake.
prompt_hi: Ek student kehta hai: 'Sarkaar sarpanch ko appoint karti hai, aur panchayat secretary ko gaon wale chunte hain.' Galti theek karo.
answer: It is the other way round: villagers elect the sarpanch; the secretary is appointed by the government.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why were seats in panchayats reserved for women and for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
prompt_hi: Panchayat mein mahilaon aur Scheduled Castes / Scheduled Tribes ke liye seats reserve kyon ki gayi?
answer: Because these groups were often left out of decision-making; reservation makes sure they have a voice and that decisions reflect the needs of everyone in the village.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: if very few villagers attend the gram sabha, what could happen to the panchayat's decisions?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar gram sabha mein bahut kam gaon wale aayein, to panchayat ke faislon ka kya ho sakta hai?
answer: Decisions might not reflect what most villagers need, and mistakes or misuse of funds may go unchecked; participation keeps the panchayat accountable.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Draw (or describe) a pyramid of Panchayati Raj with the zila parishad at the top. Write what area each level covers.
prompt_hi: Panchayati Raj ka pyramid banao (ya batao), jisme sabse upar zila parishad ho. Har star kis ilaake ko dekhta hai, likho.
answer: Top: zila parishad — the district; middle: panchayat samiti — the block (a group of villages); base: gram panchayat — a village or group of villages; under it all, the gram sabha of all adult voters.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name three kinds of work a gram panchayat does.
prompt_hi: Gram panchayat ke 3 kaam batao.
answer: Any three: drinking water, village roads, drains and cleanliness, street lights, maintaining public places, carrying out government schemes, keeping birth and death records.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Plan a gram sabha meeting in your village or area (or imagine one): name one problem to raise, one fact you would bring, and one solution you would suggest.
prompt_hi: Apne gaon ya ilaake ki ek gram sabha meeting plan karo (ya socho): ek samasya, ek tathya (fact) jo saath laaoge, aur ek samadhan batao.
answer: Any coherent plan with a local problem, a supporting fact (e.g., number of families without water) and a practical solution (e.g., repair the handpump, use a scheme for a water tank).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Explain to a city cousin how a village governs itself through Panchayati Raj.
prompt_hi: Sheher mein rehne wale cousin ko samjhao ki gaon Panchayati Raj ke zariye apna shasan kaise chalata hai.
answer: All adult voters form the gram sabha; they elect the gram panchayat (panch and sarpanch) for five years; a secretary keeps records; the panchayat handles water, roads, cleanliness and schemes; above are the panchayat samiti (block) and zila parishad (district); seats are reserved for women and SC/ST.

subject: sst
prompt_en: What is a ward, and who represents it?
prompt_hi: Ward kya hota hai, aur uska pratinidhi kaun hota hai?
answer: A ward is one of the areas a city is divided into; its people elect a councillor (corporator) to represent it.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare the mayor and the municipal commissioner: how does each get the post, and what does each do?
prompt_hi: Mayor aur municipal commissioner ko compare karo: har ek ko pad kaise milta hai, aur har ek kya karta hai?
answer: The mayor is an elected representative who heads the council of elected councillors and leads its meetings; the municipal commissioner is an officer appointed by the state government who runs the departments and day-to-day work.

subject: sst
prompt_en: A garbage pile has not been cleared in your lane for a week. Whom should you contact, and how?
prompt_hi: Tumhari gali mein ek hafte se kachre ka dher saaf nahi hua. Kise contact karna chahiye, aur kaise?
answer: The municipal body (its sanitation department) — through its helpline or app, the ward office, or the local councillor.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name four services that a municipal corporation provides.
prompt_hi: Municipal corporation ki chaar services batao.
answer: Any four: water supply, garbage collection, drains and sewers, streetlights, local roads, parks, public health/hospitals, birth and death registration, fire services.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why do city residents pay property tax?
prompt_hi: Sheher ke log property tax kyon dete hain?
answer: It pays for city services that everyone uses — water, garbage collection, streetlights, roads, parks and drains.
